title: AI Infrastructure
question: Where does the next bottleneck move?
position: Track inference cost, memory bandwidth, interconnect and power as practical constraints on AI products.
uncertainty: Which workloads will require specialised systems, and which will benefit most from general-purpose infrastructure?
signals: Cost per completed task; memory and network utilisation; deployment reliability; power availability.

history.text: Cluster interconnect, multirail networking and compute scaling form the starting point.
The archive expands into inference, reliability and distributed training.
Asynchronous compute and agent workloads connect system design to product requirements.

title: Agents & Context
question: What makes an agent useful over time?
position: Follow how context is built, edited and retained across long-horizon tasks, and how those choices change compute requirements.
uncertainty: How much improvement comes from model capability versus memory, tools and orchestration?
signals: Long-task completion; context retention; trajectory data quality; latency and cost per successful task.

history.text: Product-facing workloads and multimodal interfaces broaden the research scope.
Context engineering, agent trajectories and AI Engineer Summit material become a major research cluster.
Stateful systems, low-latency interaction and reinforcement-learning data remain tracking priorities.

title: World Models
question: How do models connect to the physical world?
position: Track the connection between multimodal understanding, spatial reconstruction and grounded interaction.
uncertainty: Which demonstrations translate into reliable products beyond controlled environments?
signals: Spatial consistency; interaction latency; generalisation; real-world evaluation and compute requirements.

history.text: World models and multimodal interfaces enter the archive.
VGGT workload analysis and 3D reconstruction remain research directions in progress.

title: Industry & Investment
question: Where will economic value accumulate?
position: Connect technical bottlenecks with industry structure, product adoption and the distribution of economic value.
uncertainty: Technical necessity does not automatically imply durable pricing power or attractive investment returns.
signals: Adoption; unit economics; competitive supply; capital intensity; valuation assumptions.

history.text: Company and deployment notes connect infrastructure research to commercial signals.
Consumer AI hardware and low-latency products expand the set of questions to follow.
